title: Course of dealing between the parties
shortTitle: Course of dealing between the parties
summary: A course of dealing is the parties’ pattern of conduct in previous transactions, used to understand their expectations in a later agreement.
notes:
A recurring way of placing, confirming, and filling orders can give a later communication significance that it would not have between strangers. American Bronze’s order-processing history is an early formation example. The later commercial-context readings examine how established dealings bear on obligations and the inclusion of terms.

Keep the time periods distinct: prior transactions supply a course of dealing; repeated conduct under the disputed contract supplies a course of performance. Both differ from practices of a wider trade. A conclusion about either requires evidence of the actual pattern and its relevance, not simply that the parties have known each other for a long time.

textbookImport.basis: Plain-language synthesis of the cited casebook passages; subject to the jurisdictional and source limits stated there.

topics.trade-usage: Prior dealings provide a party-specific source of contractual context.
